> The test for issue14046 is failing: it's because the rich text is rendered in place of the contents.

But that one looks like a pretty clear regression in readability/usability, when compared with e.g. Adobe Reader.

*Edit:* It looks like there's "\r"-strings in some of the spans in the /RC-data, but it seems that we ignore those in the XFA parser!?

> 
> 
> > The test for issue14046 is failing: it's because the rich text is rendered in place of the contents.
> 
> But that one looks like a pretty clear regression in readability/usability, when compared with e.g. Adobe Reader.

Yes it's a regression...
Just to be sure I hacked again on this pdf to change the color of the first span in the xml and the first letter of the first string in Contents, and in Acrobat, the popup clearly shows the contents when the xml is used for the editor.
And it's obvious that the popup in the pdf in #13915 is using the xml (and a Contents entry is present too).
The subtype in 14046 is `/Highlight` when it's `/Text` in 13915 (and it's `/Text` in 2966 but there are no Contents).
I don't see anything clear in the specs: my impress is that RC or Contents are almost the same, but Contents can be used for a11y stuff.
So either I missed something in the spec or Acrobat has its own specs...
And the Highlight in 13915 (for string "their squared values") is using the xml entry in Acrobat (because the X is bold).

And I noticed the `\r` (&#13;) in the xml which is confusing because it should be ignored if I understand correctly:
https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-common-syn

I played with the annotation in #14046:
 - if I change the first letter in Contents but not in RC then Contents is used;
 - if I change font-weight in RC then RC is used;
 - the color property is only shown in the editor: it has no effect in the annotation.

So my guess is:
 - RC is transformed into text, if RC_as_Text === Contents then use RC else use Contents
 - handle the &# 13; as <br>:
   - in pdf specs: `These rich text strings are fully-formed XML documents that conform to the rich text conventions specified for the XML Forms Architecture (XFA) specification`
   - in xfa specs: `XFA is fully compliant with [XML1.0]`.
 - color property is ignored in the popup which is a bit weird when it's allowed by the specs: https://www.adobe.com/content/dam/acom/en/devnet/pdf/pdfs/PDF32000_2008.pdf#G11.2097514

> And I noticed the `\r` ( ) in the xml which is confusing because it should be ignored if I understand correctly: > https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-common-syn Maybe we could simply replace line-breaking chars with `
` elements, when parsing richText in particular. Despite that being "wrong" from an XML-spec perspective, it might be what Adobe Reader does!? Also, note that we *do* support line-breaking chars for the regular /Contents entry: https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/0e7614df7f46e766237cc9a649fa6084261dce16/src/display/annotation_layer.js#L1697

I checked what we've in the xml if some spaces are added in using the editor and there are here like normal characters.
So I think that it makes sense to not skip white-spaces in general: in an editor context we want to have exactly what the user entered.
My fix will be simple:
 - not replace white-spaces by anything (trim content in onText, or replace sequence of space by one space, ...): just keep the string as it is in the xml stream.
 - use `white-space: pre-wrap` for rich text: this way we've preserve what the user entered.

We get the contents of an annotation here:
https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/0e7614df7f46e766237cc9a649fa6084261dce16/src/core/annotation.js#L361
and get it again here:
https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/0e7614df7f46e766237cc9a649fa6084261dce16/src/core/annotation.js#L2546
only if the annotation has a popup.
I've the impress that's a bit redundant, especially when we only consume this `contentsObj` in the popup element in the annotation_layer.
In my patch I follow the same scheme for the rich text so it means that we parse the xml two times...
Anyway it's something we can do in another patch (if something is wrong).
/botio test

The "regressions" are due to the fact we're using the xhtml now instead of the contents. For example in `annotation-highlight.pdf`, the xml is: ```xml

Highlight content

``` which specifies a font and a font size. I wonder if we should strip out the font-family (because Arial for example won't be available everywhere). Should we use for example Liberation to render all the annotations in order to provide the same rendering for everybody ?

> I wonder if we should strip out the font-family (because Arial for example won't be available everywhere).

That might be the simplest solution, and would ensure a more consistent handling of all PopupAnnotations regardless if they're using Contents or RichText.

> Should we use for example Liberation to render all the annotations in order to provide the same rendering for everybody ?

Unless absolutely necessary, I'd advise *against* that for overall simplicity since not all PDF.js implementations will be bundling the standard font files and we'd thus need to ensure proper fallback behaviour in that case.

issue_context.title: Incorrect rendering of annotations
issue_context.body:
Attach (recommended) or Link to PDF file here:

Configuration:
- Web browser and its version: Chrome Version 95.0.4612.0 (Official Build) canary (64-bit)
- Operating system and its version: Windows 10 Home 20H2 19042.1165
- PDF.js version: 2.9.147
- Is a browser extension: Yes

Steps to reproduce the problem:
1. Create a pdf with box annotation with formatting s.a. italics, bold, etc
2.

What is the expected behavior? (add screenshot)
1.Date and time should be set
2.Formatting should be respected (e.g., bold, italics, subscript, superscript)

mouse-over:
![pdfjs_OK](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2311076/130192780-7352f7bf-a01b-4b92-8d79-11cbed96bec9.jpg)

clicked:
![pdfjs_OK_full](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2311076/130193076-0f3b3830-5ea5-42d9-8274-472427fec133.jpg)

What went wrong? (add screenshot)
1.Date and time aren't displayed properly
2.Formatting not respected

![pdfjs_BAD](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2311076/130192847-0490f8c1-6a39-4adf-a0f1-1a9a5419afbd.jpg)

Link to a viewer (if hosted on a site other than mozilla.github.io/pdf.js or as Firefox/Chrome extension):
comments:
> Attach (recommended) or Link to PDF file here:

This part of the ISSUE_TEMPLATE is required in order for this (or any) issue to be actionable/valid.

> PDF.js version: 2.9.147

That's not an official release; please please find the latest releases at https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/getting_started/#download

> Date and time should be set

That'd suggest a *custom* implementation of the viewer, where localization isn't handled correctly (since otherwise that cannot happen).

> Formatting not respected

Given that PopupAnnotations are handled separately from the general page rendering (in the PDF.js viewer), there may be some *smaller* formatting discrepancies between e.g. Adobe Reader and the PDF.js demo viewer.

In version 2.3.164 (Official Chrome release) the result is the same.
(Chrome Version 94.0.4606.12 (Official Build) dev (64-bit))
From what I can see, pdf.js does NOT respect ANY formatting in annotations (italics, bold, subscript, superscript).

Goto page 51.
[2102.12353.pdf](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/files/7024938/2102.12353.pdf)

review_comments: Related to the comment above, I'm guessing that you might also need to "wrap" the `richText` contents into a DOM-element (and perhaps reset some CSS-rules in that wrapper) to prevent existing popup-styling from interfering with the `richText` rendering.
